articles.title: The best mouse traps that we hope you never need to buy
articles.summary: According to pest control experts, snap traps are best to help you solve a mouse problem in your home.
articles.body: It happened — you spotted a mouse. If you’re anything like me, your first instinct (after screaming) may be to pack your luggage and find a new place to live. Of course, that’s not realistic. A better option is finding a way to evict your new rodent roommate. You can certainly call a pest control company to handle the job, or you can grab the best mouse traps you can find and do it yourself (or attempt it yourself while you wait for pest control). Whatever path you choose, I collected some tips from exterminators so that you have options. I’m also sharing what they say to look for in a mouse or rodent trap, as well as tips on how to tell if you have an infestation in the first place. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best mouse traps and rodent killers of 2026 Best snap trap Both experts I spoke with recommend snap traps as the most user-friendly option on the market. These wooden traps have an indoor pedal that you put bait on — like a small piece of cheese or a schmear of peanut butter. When the mouse goes to eat the bait, it immediately triggers the bar to snap closed for quick rodent elimination, according to the brand. Best glue trap This pack comes with 36 glue traps. They are scented to attract rodents. When the mouse crawls inside the box, it gets stuck to the strong glue on the bottom, and then you can dispose of the trap and vermin. When used inside, the traps can last up to a year, according to the brand. Best electric trap Electric traps work by drawing the mouse into a tunnel (you place bait inside to attract them) and then zapping them with electricity. Each trap requires two AA batteries. The traps have a magnetic lid that you can easily pull off to dump the mouse in the trash. The electricity automatically deactivates when the lid is off to keep you safe. Best live catch-and-release trap Prefer to release your mouse once you catch it? Place bait on one side of this trap and open the trap door. When a mouse enters, the door shuts and traps the mouse. The tube-like trap has ventilation holes to keep the mouse comfortable until you’re able to release it back into the wild. Best repellent While this repellent won’t catch mice once you already have them, it can keep them away and prevent you from developing a rodent problem. These sachets are filled with cinnamon and peppermint — two scents that naturally repel rodents, according to the brand. You can place them throughout your house and garage to keep mice away. Best reusable trap These plastic snap traps are easy to clean and are intended to be reused, potentially saving you money. They have powerful springs and a large mouth to catch rodents of all sizes, according to the brand. If you do catch a mouse, the trap is designed so that you can just squeeze the end of the trap to drop the mouse in the trash. In other words, you don’t have to come in contact with the mouse. How I picked the best mouse traps and rodent killers When shopping for mouse traps and rodent killers, according to experts, there are multiple factors you should keep in mind. Here is what they suggest: Type of trap: There are a number of different types of traps on the market that can help you catch mice and rodents. Glue traps involve a sticky surface that the mouse gets stuck to, electronic zappers utilize a high-voltage electrical shock to kill rodents and live catch traps entrap mice without harming them. “There’s really nothing better than a plain snap trap, though,” says Nicole Carpenter, a pest control professional and the president at Black Pest Prevention in Charlotte, North Carolina. When a mouse steps on a snap trap, a metal hinge comes down and kills them. Cost: You’ll most likely need multiple traps to effectively capture all the mice in your home. Because of this, you’ll want to think carefully about your budget. While the electronic traps mentioned above may sound appealing, Carpenter warns that they can cost a lot more than simpler types of traps. To meet all budgetary needs, I included a range of options at varying prices. Squeamishness level: When choosing a trap, you’ll want to think about how squeamish you’ll be when having to dispose of the rodent. “With a glue trap, you’ll likely need to deal with a mouse that is alive,” says Carpenter. “With live catch traps, you’ll need to release a live mouse miles from your home — otherwise it will return.” Obviously, this is not a good option for city dwellers. With snap traps, you’ll need to dispose of a deceased mouse. What causes a mouse problem? According to experts, every house has what rodents look for — food and shelter. Of course, not every house has a mouse problem. “The real difference-maker is how easy it is for a mouse to get into a home,” says Carpenter. “If there is easy access — like gaps around doors, pipes or vents — you are literally inviting them in and telling them to make themselves comfortable.” These gaps don’t even have to be big for them to get inside, either. “Rodents utilize dime-sized openings in foundation walls and vents and garage doors as their pathways,” says Juan Rezk, chief marketing officer at Certus Pest in Tampa, Florida. “Easy food availability, like an improperly sealed pantry or an open bag of birdseed in the garage, also serves as a welcoming entrance for rodents.” How do you know if you have a mouse or rodent issue? “If you have a cat, it may notice mice before you do by staring at the same wall or sniffing around one corner,” says Carpenter. If you don’t have a cat, Carpenter says looking for droppings can help determine if mice are around. “They look like small black pellets, similar in size to grains of rice.” Another common sign you have a rodent issue: “At night, you’ll often hear wall scratching sounds,” says Rezk, who adds that even if you only see one mouse, it usually indicates there are many more somewhere. “Mice are creatures that live in social groups, and they reproduce rapidly.” Once you identify that you have a mouse problem, the first thing you should do is lock away all food sources, clean and block any entry points in your home. “Use steel wool or caulk to seal entry points around your home,” says Rezk. If you can’t locate where the rodents are getting in or the problem feels bigger than something a few traps will solve, professional assistance may be necessary. articles.title: AIG names Sierra Signorelli CEO for Americas and global insurance
articles.summary: Signorelli will take charge of AIG's commercial insurance operations across North America and Latin America & the Caribbean.
articles.body:
American International Group (AIG) has appointed Sierra Signorelli to the position of CEO, Americas and global personal insurance, with the appointment taking effect on 1 January 2027.

Signorelli will take charge of AIG's commercial insurance operations across North America and Latin America & the Caribbean, in addition to steering the group's worldwide personal insurance arm.

She will report directly to Eric Andersen, the company's president and CEO, and will become a member of AIG's executive leadership team.

Commenting on her appointment, Signorelli said: "I look forward to working with Eric, AIG's leadership team and our talented colleagues to drive the business forward, while delivering greater value for our clients and partners. That ambition is exactly why this is the right moment to return, and I am excited to be part of the company's next chapter."

The appointment marks Signorelli's return to AIG following a spell at Zurich Insurance, where she has sat on the executive committee since 2021.

During her time there, she held a series of senior positions including CEO US, CEO of commercial insurance and group chief underwriting officer.

Before joining Zurich, Signorelli spent 17 years with AIG's global specialties division, where her roles included global chief underwriting officer for specialty lines.

AIG delivers insurance products and services to corporate and individual clients across more than 200 countries and territories, operating through its own licences and authorisations as well as a network of partners.

Andersen took up the roles of president, CEO and board member on 1 June 2026, taking over from Peter Zaffino, who moved into the position of executive chair on the same date.

"Sierra's leadership and perspective will be instrumental as we continue to execute our strategy and deliver greater value to our clients and partners. I am delighted to welcome Sierra back to AIG," said Andersen.

articles.title: Why does Greenland matter to the US?
articles.summary: Donald Trump says a new deal gives the US complete control over the island’s security.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump shocked the world by threatening to seize mineral-rich Greenland by force if he could not “acquire” it or annex it.

After months of tension, a new deal between the US, Denmark and Greenland gives Washington what the president calls “permanent control” over the Arctic island’s security.

But authority still lies with Denmark. Greenlanders have protections written into the agreement, and NATO says it will still be involved.

articles.title: Veja como foi o dia dos candidatos ao governo do RS nesta quarta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha de Gabriel Souza (MDB), Juliana Brizola (PDT), Luciano Zucco (PL), Marcelo Maranata (PSDB), Priscila Voigt (UP) e Rejane de Oliveira (PSTU). Cesar Pontes (PCO) não teve agenda pública.
articles.summary: Tiveram agenda Gabriel Souza (MDB), Juliana Brizola (PDT), Luciano Zucco (PL), Marcelo Maranata (PSDB), Priscila Voigt (UP) e Rejane de Oliveira (PSTU).
articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul cumpriram compromissos de campanha nesta quarta-feira (23). Entre as atividades do dia, estiveram caminhadas com apoiadores, panfletagens e entrevistas para emissoras de rádio e televisão.

Até o dia 2 de outubro, os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul vão responder perguntas feitas diretamente por eleitores entrevistados pela RBS TV. Serão seis temas, um a cada semana: segurança, saúde, educação, infraestrutura, economia e prevenção a desastres climáticos . Ao todo, 86 eleitores terão suas dúvidas respondidas .

Os candidatos terão 30 segundos para apresentar suas respostas. Dos sete candidatos, três responderão em cada dia . A ordem de aparição leva em conta a mais recente pesquisa eleitoral contratada pelo Grupo RBS , divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24).

Rejane de Oliveira, do PSTU, distribuiu material de campanha para eleitores no Centro Histórico de Porto Alegre e apresentou suas propostas.

Sobre economia , o candidato escolheu a pergunta da eleitora Carla Ferreira. "Sou artesã e gostaria de saber qual é o plano dos candidatos ao governo de estado para o artesanato e para os agentes culturais, a cultura em si em geral, o que eles pretendem fazer para dar mais apoio e valorizar mais o artista", questiona.

"Para garantir investimento para a cultura, para o artesanato, para aquilo que a classe trabalhadora quer trabalhar, é preciso tirar o controle da economia do estado das mãos das multinacionais e colocar sobre o controle dos trabalhadores. Queremos a redução da jornada de trabalho sem redução de salário, para possibilitar mais postos de trabalho, mas também que as pessoas possam se dedicar à sua arte, às suas habilidades, que achamos de muito valor", afirmou Rejane.

Luciano Zucco, do PL, concedeu entrevistas para uma rádio e uma emissora de televisão em Porto Alegre.

Juliana Brizola, do PDT, concedeu entrevista para uma emissora de televisão em Porto Alegre.

Gabriel Souza, do MDB, realizou caminhada com apoiadores em Porto Alegre e Guaíba .

Marcelo Maranata, do PSDB, realizou uma caminhada no comércio da Zona Norte de Porto Alegre e foi a um encontro de uma confraria de negócios em Canoas .

Priscila Voigt, do UP, esteve em Porto Alegre e realizou panfletagem no bairro Restinga, na Zona Sul, e participou da greve dos estudantes do IFRS Campus Restinga.

Cesar Pontes, do PCO, não teve agenda pública.

articles.title: Crianças e adolescentes com deficiência têm prioridade em vagas no AC | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida publicada nessa terça-feira (22) também contempla filhos de pessoas com deficiência e permite a escolha de uma unidade próxima à residência ou ao local de trabalho dos responsáveis.
articles.summary: Medida publicada nessa terça (22) também contempla filhos de pessoas com deficiência e permite a escolha de uma unidade próxima à casa ou ao local de trabalho dos responsáveis.
articles.body:
Em Rio Branco, crianças e adolescentes com deficiência vão ter prioridade em vagas de escolas e creches — Foto: Reprodução/g1 Acre

Crianças e adolescentes com deficiência e filhos de pessoas com deficiência passam a ter prioridade na busca por vagas em creches e escolas públicas municipais de Rio Branco . A medida está prevista na Lei Municipal nº 2.762, sancionada em 26 de agosto e publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado (DOE) nessa terça-feira (22).

A nova lei altera uma norma de 2018 e determina que a prioridade seja aplicada na matrícula ou transferência para unidades próximas à residência ou ao local de trabalho dos responsáveis. A escolha entre essas opções ficará a cargo da família no momento da matrícula ou da transferência.

Conforme o texto, a prioridade vale para creches e escolas públicas municipais que sejam próximas à residência ou ao local de trabalho dos pais, tutores, curadores ou de outra pessoa que tenha sido nomeada judicialmente como responsável.

Na prática, a família poderá escolher se prefere uma unidade próxima de casa ou do local onde o responsável trabalha , desde que seja uma escola ou creche pública municipal.

Para comprovar o direito à prioridade, a lei estabelece que os responsáveis deverão apresentar documentos no momento da matrícula ou transferência.

documento que comprove o vínculo de trabalho.

A nova regra passou a valer na data de sua publicação.

A legislação municipal já garantia prioridade para crianças com deficiência e filhos de pessoas com deficiência desde 2018. A norma anterior previa ainda que o Poder Executivo regulamentasse a aplicação da medida.

Com a nova lei, o texto foi alterado para incluir também adolescentes com deficiência e permitir a escolha de uma unidade próxima ao local de trabalho dos responsáveis.

O número de crianças que aguardavam uma vaga em creches no Acre chegou a 2.874 , segundo levantamento divulgado em agosto de 2024 pelo Gaepe-Brasil. Os dados foram coletados junto às secretarias de Educação dos municípios.

Na época, a faixa etária com maior número de crianças na fila era a de 2 anos, com 1.229 crianças. Outras 944 tinham 3 anos, 397 tinham 1 ano, 170 tinham 4 anos e 134 tinham até 11 meses.

O levantamento mostrou ainda que 32% dos municípios acreanos tinham fila de espera. Entre as localidades que registravam crianças aguardando vaga, a falta de vagas aparecia como um dos motivos apontados.

Outro levantamento divulgado pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) na última sexta-feira (18) mostrou que 44,6% das escolas públicas do Acre tinham pelo menos um recurso de acessibilidade.

O percentual considera recursos como rampas, piso tátil e placas em braile. Entre as escolas particulares, o índice era de 97,5%.

O levantamento também apontou que apenas 29,1% das escolas públicas do estado tinham banheiro acessível para pessoas com deficiência.

articles.title: Elmano promete intercâmbio para alunos da rede pública do Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Governador e candidato à reeleição pelo PT comentou nesta quarta-feira (23) sobre novas ações para educação em eventual segundo mandato.
articles.summary: Governador e candidato à reeleição pelo PT comentou nesta quarta-feira (23) sobre novas ações para educação em eventual segundo mandato.
articles.body:
Elmano de Freitas (PT) durante caminhada no bairro João XXIII, em Fortaleza. — Foto: Fabiane de Paula / SVM

O governador e candidato à reeleição Elmano de Freitas ( PT ) prometeu, nesta quarta-feira (23), implantar um programa de intercâmbio internacional voltado aos alunos do Ensino Médio da rede pública estadual com melhor desempenho, caso seja reeleito.

A declaração ocorreu durante entrevista coletiva, logo antes de uma caminhada no bairro João XXIII, em Fortaleza. Estavam com o petista o prefeito da capital, Evandro Leitão (PT), o presidente da Câmara de Fortaleza, Leo Couto (PSB), entre outros candidatos e aliados.

A medida se soma a outras metas do gestor, como implantar em todas as escolas estaduais o modelo de ensino em tempo integral e profissionalizante , além de ampliar o número de jovens egressos da rede estadual de educação que vão para o ensino superior.

"Garantir que nós tenhamos um intercâmbio internacional, que os melhores alunos da escola pública possam fazer um intercâmbio fora do Brasil, fazer uma viagem para que com isso eles possam criar expectativas positivas e estimular o jovem no seu estudo nas nossas escolas", afirmou Elmano.

Sobre as universidades estaduais do Ceará, Elmano falou em reforçar a política de assistência estudantil e prometeu para um eventual segundo mandato concluir oito campi que estão em construção atualmente no interior do estado, entre outras ações.

"Nós queremos garantir, e vamos fazer isso, que todo campus da universidade tenha restaurante universitário, que a gente possa assim garantir uma atenção especial para o transporte escolar. Hoje isso é feito basicamente pelas prefeituras. Nós queremos fazer um investimento importante na universidade para fazer a maior política de assistência estudantil universitária do Ceará, para que o jovem da família humilde que entra na faculdade, ele possa entrar na faculdade, continue na sua faculdade e conclua o seu curso de ensino superior", prometeu o candidato.

Questionado sobre possíveis novas melhorias nos campi da Universidade Estadual do Ceará (Uece) e sobre contratações de novos professores para as universidades estaduais, Elmano respondeu que irá continuar a contratar novos docentes, sem detalhar números ou regimes de contratação.

O petista disse ainda que o maior desafio para as universidades do Estado está na política de assistência estudantil.

"A coisa mais importante para a universidade hoje, na minha opinião, é uma política de assistência estudantil, que garanta transporte, alimentação na universidade e que garanta bolsa acadêmica para esse jovem vivenciar a universidade no seu aspecto acadêmico".

articles.title: Falta de quórum faz Câmara adiar análise de projeto sobre uso de inteligência artificial em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 16 dos 33 vereadores presentes, sessão desta quarta-feira (23) foi encerrada; proposta prevê que a prefeitura informe quando IA for utilizada em serviços, documentos e procedimentos da administração pública.
articles.summary: Com 16 dos 33 vereadores presentes, sessão desta quarta-feira (23) foi encerrada; proposta prevê que a prefeitura informe quando IA for utilizada em serviços e documentos.
articles.body:
Com 16 dos 33 vereadores presentes, Câmara Municipal de Campinas (SP) encerrou a sessão desta quarta-feira (23) por falta de quórum — Foto: Câmara Municipal de Campinas

A Câmara Municipal de Campinas (SP) adiou a votação do projeto de lei que estabelece regras de transparência para o uso de inteligência artificial (IA) na administração pública municipal.

Com 16 dos 33 vereadores presentes , a sessão ordinária desta quarta-feira (23) foi encerrada por falta de quórum e nenhum dos 12 itens previstos na da pauta foram à votação. Com isso, a proposta segue em tramitação na Casa e será incluída em outra reunião.

Protocolado em fevereiro de 2025, o texto prevê que toda utilização de IA seja mencionada em local de fácil visualização sempre que qualquer órgão ou setor da prefeitura recorrer a tecnologia na execução de atividades e demandas públicas.

Segundo a proposta, o objetivo é garantir que os cidadãos saibam quando determinado serviço, documento ou procedimento contou com auxílio da tecnologia.

Na justificativa apresentada junto ao projeto, o autor afirma que o uso da IA tem potencial para aumentar a eficiência dos serviços públicos, mas também levanta desafios éticos, legais e tecnológicos.

O projeto define que a regra valerá para toda a administração pública municipal, abrangendo os setores e departamentos por meio dos quais o município exerce suas funções.

Pelo texto, sempre que houver uso de inteligência artificial, a informação deverá ser disponibilizada de forma acessível ao público.

⚠️ A proposta não estabelece restrições ao uso da tecnologia, mas cria uma obrigação de transparência sobre sua aplicação.

Também cabe ao Poder Executivo regulamentar a futura lei, caso ela seja aprovada pelos vereadores e sancionada pelo prefeito.

articles.title: SC registra segunda morte por hantavirose em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Óbito mais recente foi de um homem de 28 anos sem comorbidades, em Itajaí. Doença infecciosa grave pode levar à morte em 72 horas.
articles.summary: Óbito foi de um homem de 28 anos sem comorbidades, em Itajaí.
articles.body:
Rato-Do-Arroz (Oligoryzomys nigripes) — Foto: oliprioli / iNaturalist

Uma morte por hantavírus foi confirmada em Itajaí , no Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina . O óbito foi de um homem de 28 anos, sem comorbidades, informou a prefeitura. O caso foi confirmado também pela Diretoria de Vigilância Epidemiológica estadual (Dive) nesta quarta-feira (23).

🔎A hantavirose é uma doença infecciosa grave causada por um vírus do gênero Hantavirus e que pode levar à morte em 72 horas. É transmitida por roedores silvestres através da urina, fezes e saliva. A transmissão mais comum é pela aspiração de poeira contaminada pelo vírus.

A doença foi confirmada após exame no Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública (Lacen). A Dive informou que o paciente teve contato com urina de rato.

A morte ocorreu em 15 de setembro. O outro óbito deste ano ocorreu em Rio do Campo , no Vale do Itajaí.

articles.standfirst: Candidato do Agir ao governo do Acre prevê a criação de faculdades estaduais; banco de desenvolvimento econômico e implantação de piscinões públicos.
articles.summary: Candidato do Agir ao governo do Acre prevê a criação de faculdades estaduais; banco de desenvolvimento econômico e implantação de piscinões públicos.
articles.body:
Dr. Luisinho (Agir) apresenta propostas caso seja eleito governador do Acre — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

O candidato ao governo do Acre Dr. Luisinho (Agir) promete focar na industrialização sustentável buscando geração de empregos, atração de investimentos, valorização do servidor público e melhoria da qualidade de vida.

O plano se organiza em 10 metas de desenvolvimento econômico e diversos eixos de transformação de educação a juventude. A ideia central é integrar produção, formação profissional, financiamento e infraestrutura.

Nas áreas analisadas pelo g1 , a proposta é transformar o Acre por meio de um modelo que torne o estado um polo de produção, inovação e economia verde na Amazônia.

Infraestrutura, logística, água e energia

Agricultura, agronegócio e desenvolvimento rural

Para fortalecer a economia estadual, o candidato promete criar o Polo Industrial do Acre (PIA): distrito industrial moderno, condomínio industrial para empresas nacionais e internacionais e infraestrutura completa.

Para financiar os projetos da indústria, o candidato também propõe criar o Banco de Desenvolvimento do Acre (BDA), com crédito para indústria, agronegócio, pequenos negócios, microcrédito produtivo e crédito estudantil; juros reduzidos, acesso facilitado e gestão técnica e transparente.

Em um eventual governo, ele também pretende oferecer incentivos: cessão de terras, incentivos fiscais, crédito produtivo via BDA, apoio logístico e mão de obra qualificada.

Outro trecho do plano propõe desenvolver cadeias produtivas, como madeira/móveis, agricultura/alimentos processados, piscicultura para exportação e bioeconomia.

Por fim, Luisinho defende uma estratégia de conexão com Peru e Bolívia, acesso ao Pacífico e integração com mercados internacionais e fortalecer a agroindustrialização, a regularização fundiária, a assistência técnica e a produção sustentável.

Para a área de educação, o candidato aposta na criação da Faculdade Estadual do Polo Industrial (FEPI), que terá foco em ensino técnico e superior integrado, cursos alinhados à economia real e parcerias com empresas.

Outra instituição prevista no plano de Luisinho é a Faculdade de Medicina do Acre, com mensalidades reduzidas com subsídio do estado, financiamento acessível, parcerias público-privadas, hospitais como campo de prática, centros de simulação, interiorização da formação médica e contrapartida social.

O documento aposta em Complexos Educacionais de ensino infantil ao médio, ensino técnico e profissional, laboratórios, bibliotecas e centros de inovação.

Também são previstas medidas para financiamento educacional, como a Bolsa Esperança, com 12 mil bolsas de estudo 100% integrais para jovens e adultos de baixa renda, em áreas estratégicas como engenharia, tecnologia, energias renováveis, agroindústria, gestão, empreendedorismo, saúde e serviços essenciais.

Há ainda outros programas: Juventude do Futuro, Universidade da Indústria, Primeiro Emprego Garantido, Startup Acre, Escola do Futuro, Juventude na Gestão, Esporte, Cultura e Identidade, Conexão Digital Total, Saúde Mental Jovem e Missão Internacional.

Para o setor de saúde, Luisinho promete Complexos Regionais de Saúde e Educação – Programa “Vida Perto”, nas regiões Alto Acre, Baixo Acre, Juruá e Purus/Tarauacá-Envira, hospital completo, centro cirúrgico, UTI, maternidade, exames e diagnóstico, atendimento 24h, médicos especialistas e equipe multidisciplinar.

Por meio da tecnologia, o candidato pretende fortalecer a telemedicina, prontuário eletrônico e equipamentos modernos.

Com as medidas, o documento prevê o fim do que chama de “peregrinação por saúde”, redução de filas e atendimento regionalizado.

Luisinho promete duplicar as rodovias BR-364, BR-317, AC-10 e AC-40 e o Programa Ramal Produtivo para garantir trafegabilidade o ano inteiro, asfaltamento estratégico e patrulhas mecanizadas regionais.

O candidato também propõe universalizar agua e saneamento 24h com expansão das redes e modernização dos sistemas.

Também consta transição energética com energia solar em larga escala, usinas híbridas (solar + biomassa), biomassa como solução amazônica e autossuficiência energética para polos industriais.

A aposta de Dr. Luisinho para a habitação é o Programa Casa para Todos, com a entrega de 20 mil moradias em quatro anos, que podem ser expandidas para 40 mil em 8 anos.

Os eixos deste recorte são a construção em massa, garantia de casa e emprego, aliados a aluguel social, regularização fundiária, reforma de moradias, urbanização planejada e crédito habitacional.

O candidato pretende transformar Rio Branco na Capital Turística da Amazônia, com direito a fiação subterrânea, pavimentação em concreto, modernização de pontes, revitalização da orla do Rio Acre, centro histórico vivo, roteiros turísticos, cidade limpa e segura, mobilidade urbana e iluminação em LED.

Para isso, são previstas parcerias público-privadas (PPPs) e incentivos para hotéis, restaurantes e empreendimentos turísticos.

Com o modelo intitulado "Produzir, crescer e preservar”, o candidato prega a industrialização verde, desenvolvida por meio de manejo florestal sustentável, bioeconomia baseada em óleos, fármacos, cosméticos, alimentos e agroindústria.

Durante um eventual mandato, Luisinho pretende tratar a floresta como ativo econômico, por meio de pagamento por serviços ambientais, monetização de ativos ambientais e Fundo Solidário.

Também constam as propostas de ampliação da energia limpa, produção sustentável no campo, licenciamento ágil e responsável, combate ao desmatamento ilegal com monitoramento tecnológico e cidades sustentáveis, aliados à educação ambiental e participação popular.

O candidato promete criar o Centro de Governo como “cérebro da gestão”, com núcleos de planejamento estratégico; monitoramento e resultados, gestão orçamentária, integridade e controle, entre outros.

Luisinho também propõe a secretaria de Eficiência e Gestão, com auditoria e controle, gestão de custos, integridade/compliance, compras inteligentes, monitoramento de contratos e desburocratização.

Para garantir segurança pública, o documento prevê investir em tecnologia, inteligência policial e valorização dos profissionais, além da integração das forças de segurança, combate ao crime organizado e garantia de segurança nas áreas rurais.

Para a população do campo, o candidato promete fortalecer a agricultura familiar e o pequeno produtor, ampliando acesso a crédito, assistência técnica e agroindustrialização.

Ele também propõe incentivar sistemas agroflorestais, manejo sustentável da madeira e produção de açaí, castanha, borracha e outros ativos da floresta, conectar o campo à indústria, agregando valor à produção local.

Com foco em desenvolvimento do turismo ecológico, cultural e de aventura, Luisinho prevê o fortalecimento de políticas para gerar emprego e renda nas comunidades locais.

Entre as iniciativas estão os Piscinões do Povo: complexos públicos gratuitos de lazer aquático, com piscinas, toboáguas, áreas de descanso, alimentação, eventos, esportes e programação cultural.

As medidas preveem gestão via concessão e parceria privada, com acesso gratuito à população. A implantação ocorreria em fases, iniciando por Rio Branco, Cruzeiro do Sul e Sena Madureira, com expansão para outros municípios.

As propostas, segundo o plano, visam combater falta de lazer, violência, alcoolismo e ociosidade juvenil, além de promover saúde mental, inclusão e qualidade de vida.

O candidato apresenta o que chama de soluções definitivas para as cheias de rios e igarapés do estado com eclusas, sete lagoas artificiais e sistema de controle hídrico.

O documento promete inovar com usinas solares flutuantes e aproveitamento turístico, visando maior segurança para a população, geração de empregos e novo polo turístico.

Por fim, o projeto promete combate à pobreza com dignidade.

Para isso, o candidato afirma que irá promover inclusão produtiva, apoio a famílias vulneráveis e programas sociais integrados, além de fazer a transição do assistencialismo para o emprego.

articles.title: Key to Paul McCartney's childhood home up for sale
articles.summary: The key was sent to an American superfan of The Fab Four by the house's then-occupant in 1965.
articles.body:
A "remarkable piece of Beatles history" will go under the hammer next month at a Gloucestershire auction house.

Sir Paul McCartney lived with his family at 20 Forthlin Road, Allerton, Liverpool, for eight years until 1963, where he composed some of The Beatles' earliest songs with bandmate John Lennon.

After McCartney and, later, his brother and father moved out, a front door key and a photograph of the house was enclosed in a letter to American fan Kathy Salt from then-occupant Ashley Jones, in 1965.

The three items will be auctioned together by South Cerney auctioneers Dominic Winter on 7 October, and are expected to fetch between £2,000-£3,000.

Grieving family's £85k fundraising helps rare disease research

Warning over 'evil' fraudsters posing as police

Families fear loss of lifeline charity over £75k shortfall

McCartney moved into the council house in 1955 with his parents, Mary and Jim and his brother, Mike.

A year after the family moved in, Mary died and it was then that Jim began encouraging his son's musical development, giving him a guitar.

The living room of the house, described by current owner the National Trust as "the birthplace of the Beatles", is where McCartney and Lennon wrote "There's a Place", and "She Loves You".

Salt, who said she was a "hopelessly lovesick Beatlemaniac", was 13 when she wrote a letter to Jones from her New York home.

Replying, Jones explained he had been given two original keys to the house, where he lived with his wife, Sheila, and believed the key he was sending, may have been McCartney's own.

Six decades later, Salt said it was time to part with the key, along with other items in her collection, after a lifetime of devotion to The Beatles.

"I'm hopeful that my treasures might become someone else's to hold dear," she said.

Chris Albury, director of the auctioneers, said it was unusual to encounter a Beatles artefact "with such compelling provenance" that had such "a direct and personal connection" to the band.

"The key offers a uniquely personal connection to one of the most famous addresses in Beatles history, made all the more remarkable by the story behind its discovery," Albury said.

articles.title: UK judge refuses bail to Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal, accused of sexual assault and human trafficking
articles.summary: LONDON: A UK judge refused bail to Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal accused of sexual assault and human trafficking on Wednesday saying there was a major risk
articles.body: LONDON: A UK judge refused bail to Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal accused of sexual assault and human trafficking on Wednesday saying there was a major risk of him fleeing to avoid trial as he had no strong ties to the UK.Sasha Wass, representing Aggarwal at Southwark Crown Court, pleaded for bail saying Aggarwal is a “man of outstanding reputation” and “he is not a violent predator attacking women in streets.”“The defendant is a 57 year-old practising lawyer hugely respected in India, well known and qualified in dealing with financial crime,” Wass said.“His daughter has a 5% stake in her father’s firm. Her father is the only person qualified to deal with white collar crime,” Wass added.She proposed various bail conditions and put forward various large bail sureties amounting to a total of hundreds of thousands of pounds. These were from another lawyer Vijay Goel, a Mr Nayak, a Mr Kumar, Aggarwal’s daughter and Aggarwal himself. “He is not going to give up a high profile career in India and go on the run…He wants to clear his name,” she said, arguing that even if Aggarwal fled to India, he would be immediately put into custody and remain there until his extradition to the UK was completed.“It is fanciful to say he would interfere with witnesses,” she added. She also claimed he had various health conditions that would get better treatment in the community than at prison.Aggarwal is accused of sexually assaulting three women at a property in Mayfair who responded to job adverts for a PA between May and Aug, when he was in London on a business visa. On May 26 he asked one woman who came for a job interview if she had a boyfriend and went to the gym, touched her collarbone and tried to slide his hand down her chest, the court was told. On Aug 9 another woman was told Aggarwal was looking for “more than an assistant.” He said he wanted to feel her, hugged her and lay her on the bed and said “You should know what type of job this is.” He then kissed and sexually assaulted her on the bed, it is alleged.Extra charges of “facilitating travel for sexual exploitation” - an offence under the Modern Slavery Act 2015 - and of possessing £30k (38 lakh) as the “proceeds of criminal conduct” were on Wednesday added to the four counts of sexual assault that Aggarwal is charged with.The £30k was found on Aug 11, the day he was arrested, it is alleged.Oliver Wellings, prosecuting, objected to bail, saying: “He appears to have made contact with some 500 people and a number of interviews were conducted. The Crown’s case is he sexually assaulted at least two complainants and made sexual comments to three in highly organised systematic offending leading to grave offences against multiple complainants. Extradition from India is possible, but not certain and is a complex procedure and the Crown is concerned given the organised systematic nature of offending that he could obstruct the course of justice and interfere with witnesses if granted bail. He runs a law firm, has 30 lawyers working for him and has a partner so refusing bail has limited impact.”He said it was unclear “what knowledge Vijay Goel had” and so the Crown questioned if he was an “appropriate surety” and there were “concerns over Mr Nayak’s role as chairman of a specialist flight leasing company in connection with the defendant’s flight risks. No conditions can be attached to bail to allay the Crown’s fears,” Wellings said.Judge Alexander Milne said he did not dispute that Aggarwal had a successful and large business in India and is “apparently highly respected there” but said: “On the face of the evidence what is suggested is Aggarwal used a recruiting campaign as a sham to draw in people being offered as they understood it a job as a PA only to find that what was being sought was someone who would be sexually pliant to Aggarwal’s wishes. It reflects activity over a period of months and, on the face of it, was a deeply disturbing planned and sinister attempt to draw young women into a position where they had no choice but to comply with his sexual wishes. This suggests a man prepared to abuse status as a senior and experienced lawyer with money and power to pursue his own ends.”Refusing bail, Milne pointed out Aggarwal had no strong ties to the UK as his family, business and life are in India and took into account the “the serious nature of the allegations.”He was not persuaded it would be easy to extradite Aggarwal from India, if he fled there, saying it was “common knowledge there are many backlogs of cases in India and cases can take a lengthy period to reach court.”Aggarwal, an Indian citizen, appeared in the dock from Wandsworth prison in a grey tracksuit. His co-defendant Manpreet Kaur, who is at Bronzefield prison, did not appear on Wednesday. A plea hearing for both of them will take place later this year and a trial is scheduled for March 2027.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran’s Pezeshkian slams ‘terrorist’ US but extols diplomacy in UN speech
articles.summary: Pezeshkian leaves door open for negotiations, while calling out US blockade against Iran in Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
In a defiant speech at the United Nations General Assembly, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian has delivered a sharp rebuke to a threat by US President Donald Trump from the same rostrum the previous day to annihilate the country, but left the door open for diplomacy to end nearly seven months of war.

“The US president called us terrorists but we are the victims of terrorists,” Pezeshkian said on Wednesday.

During his speech, Pezeshkian held up a picture of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei – assassinated in a joint US-Israeli strike at the start of the war in February – as well as photos of schoolgirls killed in an alleged US air attack on their school in the southern city of Minab.

“They hit us, but we did not bow our heads or bend the knee,” Pezeshkian added.

As the Iranian president began his speech, an official from the US delegation walked out of the vast hall. The Israeli delegation also boycotted the address.

“[Trump] must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will only grow in the face of sanctions and increased pressure and bullying,” Pezeshkian said.

But Pezeshkian, a relative centrist in the Iranian ruling system, also left the door open for negotiations, saying, “Iran extends its hands towards the world.”

“We invite the world and call to it, not out of weakness, but out of a deep belief in our own power and steadfastness to cooperate and collaborate out of a deep understanding that no one in this region will have security alone,” he said.

On Tuesday, Trump said his son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who are both leading negotiations with Tehran, had held a three-hour meeting with Iranian officials.

“They had a very good meeting, a very productive meeting,” Trump told reporters at the UN, adding that he believed there was “a lot of momentum” towards an agreement. Trump later said talks were continuing and that he believed a settlement would eventually be reached.

The remarks came after Trump used his speech before UN delegates to again threaten Iran’s destruction.

“Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?” Trump said. “Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”

Addressing the US naval blockade of Iran and Tehran’s campaign to choke off trade in the Strait of Hormuz, Pezeshkian said Iran would resist what he called US efforts to use the critical sea lane to expand its war on the country.

“In the Strait of Hormuz, we cannot have some free access and gain their independence from that waterway while at the same time use that waterway to impose their aggressions upon us and to impose insecurity upon us; to forbid us access to our own waterways,” he said.

Negar Mortazavi, a senior fellow at the US-based Center for International Policy, said the Iranian president’s speech showed usual flashes of defiance, but notably signalled an appetite for a diplomatic off-ramp.

“Iran wants a way out of this war. They’ve kept the door to diplomacy open,” she told Al Jazeera.

“Reading between the lines of the Iranian president’s speech, it seems Iran may even show some flexibility as far as a return to some sort of agreement that may not be exactly along the lines of the June Memorandum of Understanding that US President Trump doesn’t seem interested in returning to,” she said. The memorandum , which has expired, called for a halt to fighting, lifting the US naval blockade and opening the Strait of Hormuz to maritime traffic.

Drawing parallels between the US and Israel bombing of Iran and Israel’s attacks in Gaza, Pezeskhian said Israel’s genocide in Gaza “revealed the double standards to which Iran is held by the international community”.

“They kill and we are sanctioned and we are punished,” Pezeshkian added.

Joey Hood, a former US diplomat and ambassador to Tunisia, said the speech leaned heavily into familiar Iranian official rhetoric and represented a lost opportunity to seek compromise.

“Instead of coming to the United Nations with something new and bold, we heard the same things that we’ve heard before,” Hood said, adding that a concrete peace offer or proposal posed to the US in the speech might have focused Washington’s attention.

“That would actually put Donald Trump on the backfoot, and he would have to respond. The Iranian president didn’t do any of that,” Hood said.

articles.title: Guatemalan man dies in crash during attempted ICE traffic stop
articles.summary: Michigan State Police and the Grand Rapids Police are investigating what led to the crash that killed Mario David Coronado Juárez, who worked as a construction worker.
articles.body: An attempted traffic stop by federal immigration officers ended in a deadly crash Sunday after the driver fled and smashed his car into a tree in Grand Rapids, Michigan, according to police. The driver, a Guatemalan national, was pronounced dead at the scene. Rosario Ovando, consul general of Guatemala in Chicago, which serves Michigan, identified the man killed in the crash as Mario David Coronado Juárez. Ovando told NBC News on Wednesday that Coronado, 36, was originally from the Guatemalan city of San Marcos. Coronado had been employed in the U.S. as a construction worker to provide for his wife and three young children, who are back in Guatemala, according to Karla Barberi and Gema Lowe, both members of the advocacy group Movimiento Cosecha in Grand Rapids. “Mario was a hard-working man for the working class. He lived a humble life. I’m showing you here who Mario is,” Lowe said, holding a picture of Coronado while speaking at a press conference Tuesday. “In his car, he only has tools to work here and just to be working for his family.” “If ICE was chasing him and caused his death, we want justice,” Barberi said. The Department of Homeland Security and ICE have not responded to requests for comment. At approximately 7:10 a.m. Sunday, Grand Rapids police responded to reports of a car that had crashed into a tree and caught fire. Coronado “was pronounced deceased at the scene,” police said in a statement Sunday. In a follow-up statement Tuesday, Grand Rapids police said, “Prior to the crash Sunday morning, Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel attempted to stop the involved vehicle and the driver fled.” Police Chief Joseph A. Trigg requested assistance from Michigan State Police in the investigation. Col. James Grady II, the state police’s director, confirmed to NBC News that the agency is “investigating what led to Sunday’s deadly crash” in collaboration with Grand Rapids police. Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer also directed the state police “to conduct an independent review of the law enforcement actions surrounding this situation,” her spokesperson, Kaylie Hanson, told NBC News in a statement. Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., sent a letter to acting ICE Director David Venturella on Tuesday requesting information about the agency’s actions in connection with Coronado’s death. “No traffic stop should end with a fatality. Something went wrong, and we need to know what and how,” Scholten said in a statement, adding that she will be demanding “a transparent investigation into facts we don’t yet know.” Scholten’s letter to Venturella demands a response by Sunday, as well as an immediate briefing on the situation. “The purpose of federal law enforcement is to make our communities safer. We must make sure that is happening,” she added. Ovando said the Guatemalan Consulate will assist Coronado’s family with the repatriation of his body whenever authorities conclude their investigation into the incident. A community vigil in Coronado’s name is planned for Thursday night at the site of the crash, according to Movimiento Cosecha in Grand Rapids. Coronado is survived by his wife, two daughters, a son and his parents, all of whom are in Guatemala.

articles.title: Barrecore and Boom Cycle owner suddenly shuts studios
articles.summary: Common Bond has emailed customers announcing its locations were closed "until further notice".
articles.body:
The fitness company behind high-end exercise classes Barrecore, Boom Cycle, and Kobox has suddenly shut all its studios.

Common Bond emailed customers announcing its locations, all of which are currently in London, were closed "until further notice".

The firm describes itself as a wellness collective and charges £2,400 for 12 months of unlimited classes. It also runs Reformcore and Triyoga brands and said in August last year it had ten sites.

Its website is no longer publicly accessible. The BBC has contacted Common Bond for comment.

The email sent to customers on Wednesday seen by the BBC said: "We're sorry to let you know that all Common Bond studios are closed until further notice.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience and disruption this may cause . We understand this is frustrating, and we appreciate your patience while we work through this."

articles.summary: Hannah Gann, dubbed the "Palestinian Rachel Dolezal," admitted in a video that she lied about being Palestinian and Black for several years.
articles.body: A Philadelphia educator known for her anti-Israel activism has admitted to lying about her Palestinian and Black identities and revealed that she is "a White woman of significant privilege and wealth" — leading some online to refer to her as the "Palestinian Rachel Dolezal." Hannah Gann, a longtime educator with the School District of Philadelphia, previously claimed that she was both Palestinian and Black, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. In one instance, her outspoken activism led to a mobile billboard that called her "Philadelphia's Leading antisemite" being parked outside her school. Inquirer journalist Kristen A. Graham wrote, "A Philadelphia teacher is being called the ‘Palestinian Rachel Dolezal’ after being caught lying about her background." This was a nod to the former NAACP official who rose to fame in 2015 after it was revealed that she had been identifying as a Black woman despite having two White parents. Graham noted that the phrase has popped up about Gann online. The Inquirer reported that Gann — a teacher at the Workshop School, a project-based high school in the School District of Philadelphia — is White and Jewish and lied about her identity for several years. FEDS OPEN PROBE INTO NEW YORK CITY'S ANTI-ISRAEL TEACHERS "Members met with Hannah and questioned her about her background on Thursday and after an hour of discussion, Hannah finally admitted she lied," the Racial Justice Organizing Committee and Philly Educators for Palestine said in a statement to the outlet, adding, "We asked her to publicly acknowledge that she is a White woman of Jewish heritage and an Israeli settler family." Fox News Digital reached out to the Racial Justice Organizing Committee. Both groups are reportedly "stunned, saddened and angered by this betrayal," and have permanently severed their ties with Gann. In a 10-minute-long video posted to Instagram, Gann admitted to and apologized for the yearslong ruse, while revealing she is "a White woman of significant privilege and wealth." FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS "There is not a single person on this planet, no friend, no fellow organizer, no one in my family, no professional connection, no secret op or handler who knew what I was doing," Gann said. "I hid my family’s background from everyone in Philly and also hid from the people in my own family what I was doing." Gann was reportedly a leading voice within the school district following the Oct. 7 Hamas-led attacks on Israel, and in 2024, she participated in a West Philadelphia "teach-in" on "scholasticide" in Gaza. She was also a vocal supporter of Keziah Ridgeway, a Philadelphia educator who was previously disciplined over pro-Palestinian social media posts shared on her private accounts. Social media posts shared by Gann in 2025 show her appearing at a public community hearing wearing a keffiyeh and speaking in an apparent accent that is not present in her apology video. According to a document compiled by the Philly Palestine Coalition (PPC) and obtained by the Inquirer, Gann allegedly made several references to having Palestinian family members. In one instance, the PPC found that a grandfather Gann claimed to be Palestinian-born was actually born in Baltimore, according to historical records. EXILED MUSLIM SCHOLAR WARNS FAR-LEFT–ISLAMIST ALLIANCE BEHIND ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTS ECHOES IRAN’S RISE Additional documents obtained by the PPC reportedly found that Gann’s family lives abroad in Israel, and that she had successfully received donations from people after telling them she was strapped for cash because she was sending money to loved ones. A University of Pennsylvania classmate of Gann’s told the outlet she was known in college "as a self-proclaimed White Jewish woman with family in the occupied West Bank. I watched her sudden transformation after she returned to Philly from the Peace Corps [in Rwanda]." The unnamed classmate reportedly added that, "she was clearly making herself look darker using makeup and fake tan, and speaking using [African American Vernacular English.]" Additionally, the PPC research document obtained by the Inquirer pointed out that Gann "is a teacher of predominantly Black youth. She has gained the trust of young people on the basis of a sense of shared oppression." BACK TO SCHOOL SHOULD NOT MEAN BACK TO FEAR FOR JEWISH STUDENTS The document reportedly alleged that Gann "has served as a mentor to at least one young White person who was manipulated by Hannah on the basis of a fake identity," and added that "her access to vulnerable young people, especially Black youth, is deeply concerning, given her pattern of lying and manipulation." In response to the allegations against Gann, the school district is reportedly providing support to students who may have been affected. CAMPUS ANTISEMITISM EXTENDS BEYOND STUDENT PROTESTS AND INTO CLASSROOMS, ADL WARNS In a statement to the Inquirer, a district spokesperson said officials are "aware of social media posts concerning a district employee and her involvement with an outside advocacy organization. These posts reference the employee’s involvement in an external group." The district, however, did not reveal whether Gann would face any disciplinary consequences for her actions, according to the outlet. Fox News Digital reached out to Gann and the Philadelphia School District. Gann’s apparent denunciation of her Israeli heritage drew the ire of the Lawfare Project, a pro bono legal organization that works to protect the rights of Jewish individuals on a global level. It’s why she believed her real identity was a liability and a fabricated identity was an asset," director of communications Jayne Zirkle said in a statement to Fox News Digital. articles.title: Three killed in separate road accidents in Greater Noida
articles.summary: Three die, three injured in separate Greater Noida road accidents: scooter hit by car then truck near Ajaibpur, mixer truck falls into canal, constable hurt.
articles.body: Noida: Three people were killed in separate road accidents in Dadri and Rabupura areas of Gautam Budh Nagar Tuesday, while three others sustained injuries, police said.In the first incident, 18-year-old Karan, was travelling with two friends, aged 16 and 17 years old, on a scooter on Tuesday evening when they were allegedly struck by a Brezza car near the bridge at Ajaibpur village. All three were thrown off the two-wheeler and Karan came under the wheels of a truck approaching from behind. Karan was killed on the spot while his friends sustained injuries and were taken to a hospital. Police said the truck driver was arrested, and a case was registered at Dadri police station.In the second accident, a driver’s aide in a concrete mixer was killed after the truck veered off the road and plunged into a canal in Rabupura late Tuesday.According to police, an NCR concrete truck was travelling towards Sector 32 when it lost control near a culvert over the Karauli canal and keeled over. It was carrying driver Amjad, and an aide Shivdesh. Police and fire brigade personnel reached the spot and pulled both out of the truck. Amjad suffered minor injuries while Shivdesh was found unconscious. He was taken to a hospital in Greater Noida where he died. Rabupura police said the body was handed over for post-mortem.In another incident, a 25-year-old police constable was injured after a car driven by a woman collided head-on with his motorcycle in Greater Noida’s Knowledge Park area Wednesday.The injured constable, Mohit Kumar, is with the traffic department. Police said the accident occurred in the afternoon when Kumar was travelling towards Sharda Roundabout on a single-lane road.Kumar suffered grievous injuries and was taken to a hospital. articles.title: In 2015, Brazilian researchers found whole forests floating through the Amazon; 40-foot trees rooted in 10-foot-deep soil with caimans beneath
articles.summary: Explore the fascinating floating islands of the Amazon, known as matupás, which host unique ecosystems and significant cultural stories. An in-depth look at their ecological importance as fishing grounds and their role in local folklore.
articles.body: In the flooded lakes of the Brazilian Amazon, some rainforest islands have spent their entire lives floating. The trees, which may grow up to 12 meters (about 39 feet) tall, have their root system firmly established in a raft of vegetation that is about 3 meters (approximately 10 feet) deep and floats on the water surface below. Matupás are considered to be important fishing grounds by local communities due to the presence of arapaima, one of the largest freshwater fish species. The local inhabitants also appreciate the fertile soil on the islands, which can be utilized for gardening or growing crops, an idea which had not been documented in the scientific literature until 2015.Scientists in Brazil released a peer-reviewed paper in the journal PLOS ONE in 2015 about the matupa, or Amazon’s floating forests, which had not been studied scientifically enough before. Instead of depending solely on aerial photographs and occasional trips to the islands, the scientists chose to go to the people who had been studying these islands since birth, the riverbank communities.Matupás form from decades of accumulated vegetationA matupá starts off merely as a collection of aquatic plants entwining themselves and floating on top of the lake surface in the floodplain. However, as time goes by, through decades, this entanglement starts to accumulate sediment and decomposed organic matter, forming a substrate thick enough to allow more complex forms of vegetation to develop from the simpler forms such as grasses and herbs to bushes and finally to complete trees. These islands are able to grow into several hectares in size, with a root ball as deep as 3 meters or 10 feet thick and a forest canopy as high as 12 meters or 40 feet high. Since the whole system is buoyant and not anchored to the lake bed, a matupá rises and falls with the water level, rather than drying out or fully flooding.Where matupás grow in the Amazon basinThis type of island is seen in the várzea lakes, which are the nutrient-rich floodplains formed by the white-water rivers carrying sediments from the Andes. It is the flow of such sediments that ensures the fertility of the várzea ecosystems and is also responsible for ensuring that matupás can create the necessary organic substratum required for the trees to grow. The study of this kind was conducted at the Reserve of Sustainable Development of Amanã in the state of Amazonas, where matupás are a familiar element of the environment, as shown by the research published in PLOS ONE in 2015.Researchers interviewed 45 residents across five communitiesThe research centered on semi-structured interviews with 45 residents across five riverine villages within the Amanã Sustainable Development Reserve. Drawing on residents' extensive firsthand experience, the researchers traced how matupás form, which species live on them, and why they matter to the surrounding communities.Residents report caimans using the islands as nesting groundOne of the most interesting facts that emerged from this survey was the extent to which local wildlife has adapted to the floating islands. Residents described caimans nesting directly on the floating vegetation, since a mature matupá's buoyancy keeps their eggs safe from the flooding that would otherwise submerge a nest on the lakebed.The matupás offer the local population more than just wildlife habitat. Community members regularly dig up the islands' decomposed organic soil for their vegetable patches, with some of the larger, more established matupás sturdy enough to grow crops directly on their surfaces.Local folklore ties the islands to a giant anacondaThe matupás also have cultural significance apart from ecological significance among the communities where research was carried out. Some people associate the islands with the story of the cobra grande, an anaconda believed to be living under the waters of the islands, which is locally revered as the spirit protector of the rivers and lakes and considered the mother of the waters. Regardless of whether the islands created this legend or not, it goes to show the extent to which the matupás have become significant within the context of these communities.A landscape hidden in plain sightThough matupás are significant not only for their sheer size but also due to their important role in nature, very little scientific research had been conducted prior to the study in question; this was due to the difficulty associated with investigating them, both through traditional fieldwork and their patchy distribution in distant lakes. As a result of drawing on the riverside communities' knowledge as scientific data, the researchers were able to build a much clearer picture of the life cycle of these floating forests, which spend most of the year adrift on the floodplain's rising and falling waters.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy calls for sustained pressure to end ‘Putin’s crazy war’
articles.summary: Ukrainian president urges world leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues to impede its war efforts.
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has singled out Russian President Vladimir Putin as the reason for the continuing war between the two neighbouring countries, urging world leaders to sustain economic pressure on Moscow during his address at the United Nations General Assembly.

“For nearly five years now, Russia’s generals have tried to carry out Putin’s crazy war,” Zelenskyy said, adding that no one openly supported this war “except for one man”.

Zelenskyy said Russia had lost 248,000 soldiers over the last eight months in Ukraine, managing to capture “a little more than 1,000 square kilometres [386 square miles] of our territory this year”.

“Putin spent 248 people for every kilometre. Does anyone still think he is smart?” he said, adding that the numbers “are not just statistics. This is about people”.

“We have archived footage of thousands and thousands of Russians losing their lives in kill zones. This is what Putin wants,” he said.

“Something always seems to stop Putin from saying, ‘That’s it. Enough. Peace,'” Zelenskyy said. “Can you even imagine him without war? He is ‘patient zero’, the one from whom war keeps spreading further. ‘Patient zero’ must be stopped,” he said.

Zelenskyy said he expects Russia to intensify its bombing campaign on the country in the coming months and that Ukrainians are prepared for a harsh winter.

“Ukrainians understand that this winter could be very harsh for us, but in response we will have no choice but to make it harsh for Russia too,” he said.

This month, Ukraine launched its deepest-ever attack into Russia, targeting two Arctic gas condensate facilities more than 3,000km (1,865 miles) from its border. Another attack on Sunday forced a Moscow oil refinery to halt crude processing.

Russia also slammed ⁠⁠jet-powered drones into two petrol stations and other sites in Kyiv, killing ⁠⁠one and injuring at least seven people on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has been pushing for an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, blaming the war between the two as one reason behind skyrocketing fuel prices.

Zelenskyy called for sustained economic pressure, saying the money Russia earned through trade “gives this war more time”.

“And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

Last week, Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia over its war in Ukraine, days after US Congress sent the bill to the White House with rare bipartisan support .

On Wednesday, Zelenskyy also claimed that nationals of 47 countries are fighting alongside Russia in Ukraine, mentioning the two North Korean soldiers captured by Ukrainian forces in Russia’s Kursk region last year, who were sent to South Korea by Kyiv.

“Why should Koreans give their lives in a war in Ukraine?” he asked.

Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Moscow is prepared to negotiate towards a lasting peace with Ukraine, but won’t just “pause” the war, arguing that such a pause would buy Ukraine and its backers time to line up more weapons.

Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says both Russia and Ukraine have expressed interest in a limited ceasefire that would halt attacks on grain shipments and each country’s energy sectors.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump’s CBP axes Biden-era policy allowing private gifts for illegal immigrants in federal custody
articles.summary: CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott ended a Biden-era policy letting the agency solicit private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody under Trump's border crackdown.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE – A Biden-era pipeline that allowed federal immigration officials to solicit and accept private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody has been shut down at U.S. Customs and Border Protection, with the agency saying the policy no longer fits the Trump administration's border crackdown. CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott withdrew the agency from the 2022 Department of Homeland Security directive effective immediately, according to an internal memo obtained exclusively by Fox News. The directive gave the leaders of CBP and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement authority to solicit, accept and use gifts related to the care of illegal immigrants held in the agencies' custody. TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94% "This delegation order is no longer needed or appropriate," Scott wrote. "With the significant decrease in encounters and apprehensions, CBP no longer requires private donations or gifts for distribution to aliens in custody." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY Scott said the policy also "does not align with the Trump administration's strengthened enforcement posture at our borders and related presidential actions issued by the administration." "For these reasons, I am withdrawing CBP from DHS Delegation 07107, Rev. 1 effective immediately," he wrote. CBP TOUTS HISTORIC MILESTONE, PUSHES FOR EVEN LARGER WORKFORCE: 'WE AREN’T STOPPING HERE' CBP confirmed the move to Fox News and said officials recently discovered the directive and moved to rescind the agency's participation. The withdrawal applies to CBP; Scott's memo does not say ICE has been removed from the DHS policy. The original delegation was signed May 3, 2022, by then-Deputy Homeland Security Secretary John K. Tien. DHS BUYS TWO CALIFORNIA MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS FOR $1.5B TO BOOST ICE DEPORTATION CAPACITY The order also authorized the CBP commissioner and ICE director to solicit specific gifts related to the care of illegal immigrants in custody. Scott said CBP sought the authority because of the "elevated number of aliens encountered, processed and held" in its facilities at the time. He wrote that the significant decrease in encounters and apprehensions means CBP no longer needs private donations or gifts to distribute to migrants in custody. articles.title: As major powers act unilaterally, experts say UN faces crisis in New York
articles.summary: Experts warn the UN faces crises of funding, relevance, and Security Council gridlock.
articles.body:
As world leaders gather in New York for the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), experts say the institution is battling an existential crisis of funding, relevance and Security Council gridlock.

Major conflicts appear intractable, and powers like the United States and Russia can bend the UN’s Security Council to their will; member states are looking for new mechanisms to bring accountability to the venue and for a new secretary-general to voice their concerns. The body has been accused of failing to stop what its own experts have said is a genocide in Gaza.

World leaders are not under any illusion that the UNGA is in good health, said Daniel Forti, head of UN Affairs at the International Crisis Group. Yet many still understand the venue’s power.

“The vast majority of leaders, from small states, from middle powers, and even a few from major powers, recognise the importance of a UN that is a global conversation platform,” Forti said.

Trying to weigh in where the Security Council fails

The UN is juggling multiple conflicts – from high-profile wars involving Iran to the often overlooked catastrophes in Sudan and Myanmar .

In the Ukraine war, the UN says more civilians were killed in the first eight months of 2026 than in the whole of 2025, and even NATO powers now say they worry about spillover into their countries.

Russia has repeatedly vetoed Security Council resolutions, but Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has continued to appear before the UNGA to urge member states to help stop Moscow.

On Wednesday, Zelenskyy spoke for the fifth time before the assembly since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, urging leaders to further tighten economic measures meant to punish Moscow despite its vetoes of Security Council resolutions.

“Many of you here have seen more than once how the abuse of the veto at the UN weakens the world and pushes peace further away,” Zelenskyy said.

In the Israeli war on Gaza, the UN has labelled Israel’s conduct there a genocide , but it has struggled to exercise real agency. Security Council resolutions have been repeatedly vetoed, and UN relief agencies have been targeted by Israel without any accountability.

The ongoing war between the US, Israel and Iran is having economic impacts across the globe and threatens to plunge Yemen back into a civil war.

“From Ukraine, to Gaza, and Sudan, and also with what’s happening now in Iran, the veto problem leaves the UN hamstrung,” said Alanna O’Malley, professor and chair of Global Governance and Wealth and head of the Department of History at Erasmus University.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told Al Jazeera’s James Bays this week that these conflicts were having real humanitarian impacts worldwide, including reduced food access, rising fuel prices, and global inflation.

The UNGA will allow the opportunity for some discussions for parties involved in these kinds of conflicts, but it is unlikely they can reach major agreements, said Forti.

But the assembly is still the only forum where all 193 member states are equal, and nations have tried to invoke new procedures and reach back into historical mechanisms to try and mitigate the veto deadlocks, O’Malley said.

A 1950 resolution, dating from a deadlock over the Korean War, has allowed the UNGA to debate issues vetoed in the Security Council. And in 2022, an impasse over Ukraine generated a new mechanism forcing any permanent council representative – China, France, Russia, the UK, and the US, often called the P5 – to come before the UNGA and explain when it uses the veto.

“The idea is to build more accountability into the system for the P5, to make the veto not just harder to use, but also ensure it uses a lot of political capital,” O’Malley said.

Calls for reforms have only increased since 2023 and Israel’s war on Gaza, O’Malley said, with “unprecedented” majority votes in the UNGA challenging the Security Council.

Perhaps the greatest challenge facing the UNGA, though, is remaining relevant as major global powers go their own way.

The administration of US President Trump has pushed through its own Board of Peace, a body that has accomplished few of its goals but has secured Security Council approval and claims to take on responsibilities previously handled by UN agencies, like distributing aid or managing refugees.

Unhappy with the UN, Trump has also imposed sanctions on the body’s special rapporteurs, as well as organisations like the International Criminal Court.

Washington, though, may not be the only government looking to strike out on its own.

Chinese President Xi Jinping is in the US this week, but he will not be attending the UNGA. He last addressed the body in 2021 via video, but this year he will skip it altogether, opting instead for one-on-one talks with US President Trump. China has positive views of the UN, often using the Security Council to weigh in on global issues, Forti said, but it is also looking for alternatives, through venues like BRICS and the SCO, to strengthen multilateralism.

The impetus to look for alternatives to the UN, even Secretary Guterres admits, is driven by the fact that the Security Council is unable to pass binding resolutions in the most controversial situations, because permanent members can simply veto them based on their own interests.

Guterres told Al Jazeera this week that kind of inaction was creating an “environment of impunity”, where the behaviour of major global powers was inspiring middle powers and others to “believe that they can do whatever they want because nothing will happen to them”.

The search for the next secretary-general

Guterres’s term ends on December 31, and the Security Council is expected to announce its recommendation for who will replace him.

“We had a secretary-general who didn’t have a lot of political capital to expend to solve these conflicts, and he hasn’t taken great initiative on a lot of them,” said O’Malley.

Guterres did, for example, draw on rarely used Article 99 powers in 2023 to bring the Gaza issue before the Security Council. But the UN also faces major funding problems, with major donors like the US cutting back, making it difficult to deliver aid in places like the West Bank and Gaza. “So he [Guterres] also has no actual financial capital,” O’Malley said.

Candidates to replace Guterres must win at least nine of the 15 votes from the council, and avoid a veto by any of the P5, to be put before the UNGA for a vote.

Forti said member states are looking for someone to refocus on preventing wars, and also deal with criticism that the UN has become unwieldy and costly.

“They will have to balance the UN’s diplomatic work, its impact, with financial cuts and racing to the bottom,” Forti said.

articles.title: US visa: Immigration lawyer says Green Card lottery, visa processing for 75 banned countries did not resume despite court order
articles.summary: Two US visa processing pauses challenged in federal court have been struck down, but affected applicants are still waiting for their cases to move
articles.body: Two US visa processing pauses challenged in federal court have been struck down, but affected applicants are still waiting for their cases to move forward, according to an immigration lawyer who says there is a growing gap between the court rulings and what applicants are experiencing at US embassies and consulates. Jennifer Bade, an immigration attorney and owner of Bade Law Group, said in a LinkedIn post that the State Department had paused visa processing for two groups over the past year — Diversity Visa applicants and immigrant visa applicants from 75 countries.Both pauses got challenged in federal court and both got ruled out. The State Department acknowledged the ruling but there has been no movement in reality.A federal judge on August 21 struck down the 75-country immigrant visa pause, while another federal judge on August 28 ruled against the Diversity Visa pause. The State Department acknowledged the court rulings and said the two pauses were no longer in effect."But here's the problem: Acknowledging a court order and actually following it are two different things," Bade said.Giving a picture of the reality, the attorney said that families with scheduled interviews found that their interviews were canceled with no explanation and no new date. Bade said when lawyers pushed back in court, the government used a loophole and said these interviews were not canceled but would be rescheduled."Embassies weren't telling anyone when, or if, their case would move again. It just became stale," she said."It took almost three more weeks for the State Department to formally instruct its embassies and consulates to resume processing. That instruction went out on September 10. Even now, most consular posts haven't shown any real movement. A handful overseas have started processing again. For most applicants, there's still no visa issued and no rescheduled interview," Bade said.Green Card lottery (Diversity visa) applicants face a particular deadlineIf you're a Diversity Visa selectee for this year, this matters even more, the attorney explained. "The law does not allow any extra time. If your visa isn't issued by September 30, your selection expires. It cannot roll over to next year."That means a person selected in the lottery does not simply retain the selection and carry it into the following year if the visa is not issued by the deadline."If you or a family member has a pending immigrant visa or Diversity Visa case that was affected by either pause, now is the time to follow up directly with the consulate and document everything, every email, every response, every date," she said.What is Green Card lottery?The Diversity Visa (DV) programme, commonly called the US green card lottery, is an annual US immigration programme for people from countries that have historically had relatively low levels of immigration to the US. So this program is not from people from India and China as they have higher immigration to the US.Each year, the State Department conducts a lottery among eligible applicants. Those selected can apply for immigrant visas — essentially a route to US permanent residence (green cards) — if they meet all the eligibility requirements.Congress has authorised up to 55,000 DV visas a year, although the actual number available can be lower. No single country can receive more than 7% of the available visas in a fiscal year.The State Department announced a pause in Diversity Visa issuance in December 2025. This was not a cancellation of the lottery itself. Applicants could still submit applications and attend interviews, but the State Department said no Diversity Visas would be issued during the pause. The administration said it was reviewing the programme's screening and vetting procedures following the Brown University shooting and the killing of an MIT professor, which officials said involved an individual who had previously been admitted to the US through the DV program.You use AI every day.
